title: Magnets Pull Some Things
keyIdea: A magnet pulls, or attracts, some things to it. It pulls things made of iron or steel, like paper clips, pins and bolts. It does not pull paper, cloth, wood or plastic, and it does not pull every metal: gold and brass are not pulled. A magnet pulls best close up, and it can pull through thin paper.

kid: A magnet can pull some things to it. Hold it near a paper clip. Click! The clip jumps to the magnet.
A magnet does not pull a sock. It does not pull paper or wood. They stay still.
A magnet pulls things made of iron or steel. A pin is steel. A bolt is steel. Gold and brass are metal too, but a magnet does not pull them.
A magnet pulls best when it is close. Far away, it may not pull at all. It can even pull through thin paper.
adult: Early years science and the English national curriculum both start magnets with hands-on play. Year 3 then asks pupils to 'observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others' and to 'compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials'. In the US, kindergarten pushes and pulls lead to 3-PS2-3 on magnetic forces.

A magnet attracts magnetic materials: iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. Everyday magnetic things are mostly iron or steel, such as paper clips, safety pins, bolts and food tins. Paper, cloth, wood and plastic are not attracted. Neither are most other metals, including gold, brass, copper and aluminium. The pull is a non-contact force: it acts across a gap and through thin paper, and it gets weaker quickly with distance.

Common mistakes: thinking a magnet pulls every metal, or anything shiny; thinking it pulls anything at all, such as paper or a sock; believing paper or a table blocks the pull; and thinking a bigger or redder magnet is always stronger. Be careful with coins and keys, which may or may not be steel. Test them rather than guess.

In the lab your child tries a magnet on six things, fishes for the three fish that carry a paper clip, drags a magnet under paper to pull a clip home, moves a magnet closer until the clip jumps, and predicts whether a tin can, gold ring, scissors and a trumpet will be pulled.

familyTip: Go on a magnet hunt round the kitchen with a fridge magnet. Before each test, ask 'Will it pull?' Then try it. Fridge doors and tins usually pull; wooden spoons and plastic boxes do not.

visual.caption: Will the magnet pull it? Drag each thing into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: try a magnet on six things, go magnet fishing, pull a clip through paper, move the magnet closer, and test four metal things.

practice.prompt: The magnet pulls {a} paper clips and {b} pins. How many things did it pull?
practice.hint: Count the clips. Then count on the pins.
practice.explain: Clips and pins are both steel, so the magnet pulls all of them: {a} and {b} more make {=a+b}.

practice.prompt: There are {a} fish. Only 2 have a paper clip. How many fish will the magnet not catch?
practice.hint: Fish with no clip are not pulled. Take away the 2 with clips.
practice.explain: The magnet only catches the 2 fish with clips. {a} take away 2 is {=a-2} fish it will not catch.

practice.prompt: You test {a} socks and {b} pins with a magnet. How many things does it pull?
practice.hint: Does a magnet pull cloth? Does it pull steel pins?
practice.explain: Socks are cloth, so none of them are pulled. The {b} pins are steel, so the magnet pulls {b} things.

practice.prompt: Which one will a magnet pull?
practice.hint: Which one is made of steel?
practice.explain: A safety pin is steel, so the magnet pulls it. A sock is cloth and a block is wood: no pull.

pool.prompt: A magnet pulls {a} pins and {b} bolts. How many things did it pull?
pool.hint: Pins and bolts are both steel. Add them.
pool.explain: Pins and bolts are steel, so all of them are pulled: {a} and {b} more make {=a+b}.

pool.prompt: A box has {a} paper clips and 3 crayons. How many things will a magnet pull out?
pool.hint: Crayons are wax. Which things are steel?
pool.explain: Only the {a} paper clips are steel, so the magnet pulls out {a}. Crayons are not pulled.

pool.prompt: Which one will a magnet NOT pull?
pool.hint: Two are steel. Which one is not?
pool.explain: Paper is not pulled. The paper clip and bolt are steel, so the magnet pulls them.

pool.prompt: Does a magnet pull all metal things?
pool.hint: Think of the gold ring and the trumpet. Were they pulled?
pool.explain: A magnet pulls iron and steel, but not every metal. Gold and brass are not pulled.

pool.prompt: Paper is between a magnet and a clip. What happens?
choices: The magnet still pulls the clip
The paper sticks to the magnet
pool.hint: Remember the clip that went home.
pool.explain: A magnet can pull through thin paper, so the clip still moves. The paper itself is not pulled.

pool.prompt: When does a magnet pull a paper clip best?
pool.hint: What happened when you moved the magnet closer?
pool.explain: The pull is strongest close up. Far away it may not pull at all. Colour does not matter.

pool.prompt: A gold ring is metal. Will a magnet pull it?
pool.explain: Gold is a metal, but magnets do not pull gold. They pull iron and steel.
